designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Instantly readable joke with broad appeal (every driver gets it), clean consistent line icons and a strong bold punchline that carries from across a room; the 4x5 grid looks like a real dash legend. Weak spots: the tiny condensed labels vanish on the tee and turn into noise, and a few icons are muddled (washer fluid has a stray diagonal slash, glow plug and brake-pad-wear read as abstract squiggle/circle).
designs.fix: Enlarge the whole print on the chest and bump the labels up at least 30% (or drop to 16 icons so each label can grow), and redraw the washer-fluid icon cleanly.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The strongest of the three: warm, expressive brush dogs, a perfectly timed repetition gag (Turn around x4) that pays off with 7. Sigh., and an elegant serif type treatment that feels giftable and premium at $50; works on both tees. Downsides: the print sits small and airy on the shirt so the italic captions get too fine to read at a glance, and the lone tiny moon under the title looks like a stray mark.
designs.fix: Scale the print up and tighten the vertical spacing so the dogs and captions are bigger on the tee, and make the moon larger or drop it.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Universal cat-owner joke told cleanly in three wordless panels, with nice detailed tabby linework and a smug payoff face in panel 3. But it is a very familiar gag, and the execution has visible errors: in panel 2 the arm lines run past the right edge of the frame and stop abruptly in empty space, the 1 numeral is an odd flag-shaped glyph that does not match the 2 and 3, and the dense hatching on the cat will fill in on a one-ink print at this small size.
designs.fix: Fix panel 2 so the arms are cleanly clipped at the frame (or deliberately break the frame like panel 3 does), and redraw the 1 to match the other numerals.
